2. Short facts which are necessary for disposal of the rule are that the present Petitioner as Plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 48 of 1983 in the Court of Sub-Ordinate Judge, Habiganj, praying for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession to the suit land and for further declaration that the suit property is not vested property as declared vide V.P. Case No. 12/81-82 dated 20.9.1981. During pendency of the suit one Mr. AKM Fazlul Huq was transposed as Plaintiff No. 2 in the suit. 

 12. It is the only question has to be decided by this Court as to whether the appeal stood abated as a whole on account of failure to substitute the heirs and legal representatives of the Respondent No. 2 (Plaintiff No. 2). It appears that the suit was for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and for further declaration that the suit property was not a vested property. The share of the Plaintiff No. 1 and 2 has not been specified in the suit. A common question of law raised in the case of Raghunath Singh Hazari and others Vs. Abdul Rashid, reported in 8 DLR 577 and in the case of Wali and others Vs. Manak Ali and others, reported in 17 DLR (SC) 536 and also in the cast., law reported in 27 DLR 62 and it has been held that the appeal stood abated as a whole on considering unspecified share of the Plaintiffs. Those decisions are applicable in the instant case. So I hold that the learned Additional District Judge has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in deciding the question of abatement in the appeal. The impugned orders are not sustainable in law.
